parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime offers a trans visitor no criminalisation of trans identity, but also no statutory remedy, no hate-crime enhancement, and a judiciary documented as non-functional as a protection avenue. Documented exposure is social rather than state-imposed: a 2018 official assessment found hostility toward visible LGBTI people, above-average in the capital; single unresolved incidents (2019 advocacy-president death, 2010 camp harassment) are dated and thin. Pending 2017 bills carrying three years' imprisonment for public advocacy have unverified status and are largely resident-facing. No border-document, facility or custody rule is documented — absence of evidence, not safety. Severity if outed is discrimination, harassment and possible violence with no working recourse; imprisonment is not a credible documented outcome. Thin data extrapolated from weak rule of law plus documented hostility lands mid-Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. The record explicitly does not address passport or ID gender markers, visa screening, or airport/border treatment linked to gender presentation.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No documented acceptance of X markers or presentation-document mismatch for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown whether document mismatch would trigger secondary screening; no state practice documented either way.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No custody rule documented: no birth-sex housing, segregation or strip-search practice recorded. Pending 2017 advocacy bill (3 years) status unverified after Nov 2017.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No consular, legal-aid or release mechanism recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch or public visibility could in principle feed an investigation, but no such pathway is sourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward, shelter or changing-room rule appears for visitors; 2010 camp harassment is disaster-context and dated.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Disaster-response denial of housing/healthcare was reported for gay and bisexual men in 2010; no later or trans-specific instance sourced.

care_services.exposure: Constitutional health, housing and food guarantees extend to citizens only, so a visitor cannot invoke them; health baseline figures date from 2008 and are general-population.
care_services.protection: Not documented. No anti-discrimination coverage of gender identity in services; community HIV organisations serve residents.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care or HIV-related need could force disclosure with no enforceable refusal remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2018 official assessment: hostility toward public, visible LGBTI people, particularly in the capital; pending bills framing public advocacy as punishable; no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct since 1791 (climate signal only); no trans-specific offence documented in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostility is societal, but state supplies no protection, so a confrontation has no working official backstop.

minors_guardians.exposure: Good-conduct certificate denial on homosexuality grounds would affect resident students and young workers, not a visiting guardian; nothing documents treatment of a travelling minor or accompanying trans parent.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family shares the undocumented border/facility gaps; no minor-specific rule sourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Single unresolved incident: national LGBTQ advocacy president found dead 2019, poisoning reported but unconfirmed; dated 2010 displacement-camp harassment of transgender people. No pattern, counts or state-implicated custody violence documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; regional LGBTQ group statements show civil society, not visitor recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No record of police response to anti-LGBTI violence either way; hostility report suggests thin recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory remedy, no hate-crime enhancement, judiciary documented as not functioning in practice; record stops Nov 2017 on the pending bills, so current law is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: External monitors only (2018 reports, 2019 mourning statement); no domestic institutional guidance for trans travellers.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse converts every documented social-hostility exposure into an unremediable one.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower exposure than 0.35-A: no Visitor Conduct Register, entry bar, or routine state exclusion mechanism is documented here. The dossier's worst feature is dated social hostility plus absent recourse, not a universal state-imposed exclusion applied at every crossing, so it sits materially above this tier-1 anchor.

Higher exposure than 0.55-B: that anchor has an administrative screening regime but working written decisions, appeal desks and consular notification. Here the dossier states no statutory remedy exists and the judiciary does not function, so the same level of friction would leave the traveller worse off despite fewer documented mechanisms.

Below 0.65-A: that anchor rests on national equality law, intervention by an advocacy group, an accountability board that apologised and compensated, and courts that reliably order release. This dossier documents the opposite institutional posture — no equality law, no hate-crime enhancement, non-functional judiciary — while lacking the anchor's documented detention incident.

Comparable: both feature durable exposure to officials through documentation or visibility, harassment and service loss as the typical harm, no credible execution threat, and an oversight body that is slow or absent. This dossier documents less mechanism (nothing on registration) but equally thin recourse, so mid-0.45 fits.

parsed.synthesis: The regime combines documented social hostility toward visibly LGBTI people (2018, the most recent official climate assessment in the record), an institutionally absent remedy set (no anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime enhancement, non-functional judiciary), and no documented state-imposed universal exposure at borders, facilities or custody — those gaps are unanswered questions, not evidence of safety. Single dated incidents (2019 unresolved advocacy-president death, 2010 camp harassment) show severity potential but not frequency or state direction. Pending 2017 bills criminalising public advocacy are unverified past November 2017, so they are a climate signal, not operative law. Absence of criminalisation of trans identity keeps this out of the high-risk bands; absent recourse plus hostile climate keeps it out of reduced risk. Travelling minors inherit the same undocumented gaps.
